data.cultural_impact: The name Sharvansheem holds a significant cultural impact in Hindu traditions as it is associated with Lord Shiva, one of the primary deities worshipped in Hinduism. Lord Shiva is revered as the god of destruction, transformation, and regeneration. He is often depicted as the eternal Prakriti Purush or the embodiment of pure Shiva consciousness. The name Sharvansheem pays homage to this powerful deity, signifying respect and devotion towards him and the profound influence of Hindu mythology on Indian culture.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Sharvansheem holds immense spiritual significance for Hindus as it symbolizes the idea of surrendering oneself to the divine will of Lord Shiva. Just as the king has absolute power and jurisdiction over his subjects, Lord Shiva is believed to be the absolute ruler of all creation. By invoking the name Sharvansheem, one seeks Lord Shiva's blessings, protection, and guidance in life's journey. The name is a constant reminder of the existence of a higher power and the importance of spirituality in human life.

historical_references.reference: The Sharvansheem dynasty ruled the ancient Indian kingdom of Magadha from the 6th century BCE to the 4th century BCE.

trends: The name Sharvansheem is not commonly used in modern times.
